paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取更新。

articles.title: This October is on track to be the hottest ever recorded

paras.en: This October is almost certainly going to be the hottest October ever recorded. Global temperatures this month are set to be around 1.76 degrees Celsius (about 3.17 degrees Fahrenheit) above preindustrial levels, surpassing the previous record set in 2023, researchers predict.
paras.zh: 几乎可以肯定，今年十月将是有记录以来最热的十月。研究人员预测，本月全球气温将比工业化前水平高出约 1.76 摄氏度（约 3.17 华氏度），超过 2023 年创下的纪录。

paras.en: An especially hot October also puts 2026 on track to be among the hottest years ever recorded—if not the hottest—according to projections from climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather. Their projection is based on data collected by the Europe-based Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S).
paras.zh: 根据气候科学家安德鲁·德斯勒 (Andrew Dessler) 和泽克·豪斯法瑟 (Zeke Hausfather) 的预测，特别炎热的 10 月也将使 2026 年成为有记录以来最热的年份之一（即使不是最热的）。他们的预测基于欧洲哥白尼气候变化服务（C3S）收集的数据。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Next year could be even more blistering. “This year’s record-setting October is a sign that the ‘Super El Niño’ is kicking into gear and will likely be the first in a series of record-setting months, culminating in a record-setting 2027,” Hausfather says.
paras.zh: 明年可能会更加激烈。 Hausfather 表示：“今年创纪录的 10 月是‘超级厄尔尼诺现象’即将启动的一个迹象，并且很可能是一系列创纪录月份中的第一个，并在 2027 年达到创纪录的顶峰。”

paras.en: El Niño is a cyclic climate pattern that occurs when part of the Pacific Ocean is unusually warm, affecting weather across the world. El Niño can exacerbate climate change—which is driven by the burning of fossil fuels—to boost global temperatures.
paras.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象是一种周期性气候模式，当太平洋部分地区异常温暖时就会发生，影响世界各地的天气。厄尔尼诺现象会加剧由化石燃料燃烧引起的气候变化，从而提高全球气温。

paras.en: In 2023, also an El Niño year, October temperatures reached 1.7 degrees C (3.06 degrees F) above preindustrial levels, according to Dessler and Hausfather’s analysis. The year was the hottest ever recorded at the time, after which it was surpassed by 2024. The following year, 2025, was the third-hottest year ever recorded.
paras.zh: 根据德斯勒和豪斯法瑟的分析，2023 年也是厄尔尼诺现象年，10 月气温比工业化前水平高出 1.7 摄氏度（3.06 华氏度）。这一年是当时有记录以来最热的一年，之后到 2024 年就超过了这一年。次年，即 2025 年，是有记录以来第三热的一年。

paras.en: October’s likely record follows several other superlative moments so far in 2026, including the U.S.’s hottest September, hottest first eight months and hottest 12-month period ever recorded, as well as the hottest global ocean temperatures ever recorded.
paras.zh: 10 月可能创下的纪录是在 2026 年迄今为止的几个最热时刻之后发生的，包括美国有记录以来最热的 9 月、最热的前 8 个月和最热的 12 个月，以及有记录以来最热的全球海洋温度。

articles.title: ‘Paleo lighting’ can fix your brain’s clock after daylight savings

paras.en: At 2 A.M. on November 1, the clocks will fall back, and for one weekend out of the year, the whole country will think about light and time. Most people will spend the extra hour asleep and the following week complaining that it’s nearly dark at 5 P.M. Regardless of how you feel about the time change, for the next four months the sun will rise in the sky closer to the time you do. That alignment is the best thing that could happen to your body clock—and your sleep—all year.
paras.zh: 凌晨 2 点11 月 1 日，时钟将倒退，一年中的一个周末，整个国家都会思考光和时间。大多数人会多睡一个小时，然后在接下来的一周里抱怨下午 5 点天就快黑了。无论您对时间变化有何感受，在接下来的四个月里，太阳在天空中升起的时间将会更接近您的升起时间。这种调整是全年对您的生物钟和睡眠可能发生的最好的事情。

paras.en: Of course, you can try to buy your way into a better night’s sleep right now: mouth tape, tablets of magnesium glycinate, blackout curtains, a wearable sensor that grades your sleep, a mattress that maintains a chill 62-degree-Fahrenheit temperature. The stack of such approaches can run into the thousands of dollars and has a name on social media—“sleep maxxing.” It’s the wellness market’s latest way of turning a basic human function into a product line.
paras.zh: 当然，您现在就可以尝试通过购买方式获得更好的睡眠：口腔胶带、甘氨酸镁片剂、遮光窗帘、可对您的睡眠进行分级的可穿戴传感器、保持 62 华氏度低温的床垫。这些方法的成本可能高达数千美元，并且在社交媒体上有一个名字——“睡眠最大化”。这是健康市场将人类基本功能转变为产品线的最新方式。

paras.en: But the two things that will do the most for your sleep cost nothing. That is because nobody has figured out how to package them.
paras.zh: 但对你的睡眠最有帮助的两件事是免费的。那是因为没有人知道如何包装它们。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: I’m talking about light: bright days, dark nights. Think of it as a return to nature. Call it Paleo lighting.
paras.zh: 我说的是光：明亮的白天，黑暗的夜晚。将其视为回归自然。称之为古照明。

paras.en: I shamelessly borrowed the term from the “Paleo diet,” which sold the premise that human physiology took shape under conditions that no longer exist and that the mismatch costs us something. We built an industry around what goes into our mouths. We left the eyes alone. Our ancestors could not dim the day, postpone the night, or order light at midnight. That is not an argument for candlelight or for unplugging the grid. It is the same dietary logic aimed at the organ that sets our internal clock.
paras.zh: 我无耻地从“古饮食”中借用了这个术语，它的前提是人类生理学是在不再存在的条件下形成的，而这种不匹配会让我们付出一些代价。我们围绕进入我们嘴里的东西建立了一个产业。我们留下了眼睛。我们的祖先无法调暗白天，推迟夜晚，或在午夜点灯。这并不是支持烛光或拔掉电网的理由。这与针对设定我们体内时钟的器官的饮食逻辑相同。

paras.en: This clock sits at the base of the brain, about 40,000 nerve cells in a structure called the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) in the hypothalamus, and it generally runs slightly long. Shut a person in a laboratory with no windows and no clocks, and typically the body settles into a day of roughly 24 hours and 12 minutes.
paras.zh: 这个时钟位于大脑底部，下丘脑中称为视交叉上核 (SCN) 的结构中约有 40,000 个神经细胞，并且它的运行时间通常稍长。将一个人关在没有窗户、没有时钟的实验室里，身体通常会适应大约 24 小时 12 分钟的一天。

paras.en: Light early in the morning is what pulls the clock back in line with the sun. Bright light at night does the opposite, telling it the day isn’t finished. And the clock in your head is not the only clock you own. Your liver, pancreas and immune cells all run on their own daily schedules, taking their cues from that cluster of cells in the hypothalamus linked to the sun. When the SCN loses alignment with the sun, these rhythms drift apart and optimal functioning may be lost.
paras.zh: 清晨的光线使时钟与太阳保持一致。夜晚的明亮光线则相反，告诉它这一天还没有结束。而且你头脑中的时钟并不是你拥有的唯一时钟。你的肝脏、胰腺和免疫细胞都按照自己的日常时间表运行，从下丘脑中与太阳相关的细胞群中获取线索。当视交叉上核与太阳失去对准时，这些节律就会偏离，并且可能会失去最佳功能。

paras.en: The disruption to our circadian rhythms comes at a physiological price. Light at the wrong hour can suppress melatonin, the hormone that tells your body it is night. And from there, the effects may spread to digestion, heart rate and the timing of metabolic and immune programs evolved to run on a 24-hour schedule. How far that reach extends is still being mapped. The clearest view comes from animals, for which you can hold everything else steady and change only the light.
paras.zh: 我们的昼夜节律被破坏是要付出生理代价的。错误时间的光照会抑制褪黑激素的分泌，褪黑激素是一种告诉身体现在是晚上的激素。从那时起，影响可能会蔓延到消化、心率以及代谢和免疫程序的时间安排，进化为按 24 小时计划运行。该范围的延伸范围仍在绘制中。最清晰的视野来自动物，为此你可以保持其他一切稳定，只改变光线。

paras.en: In my laboratory, we have kept mice at night with lights set to five lux, roughly the brightness of a night-light in a kid’s bedroom. They gained more weight than mice sleeping in genuine darkness. They were not sleep-deprived; the night-light just disrupted their clock-gene rhythms, subsequently shifting their food intake to the wrong part of the day. In the case of nocturnal mice, they shifted their food intake from night to daytime. Because they generally sleep during the day, light at night can scramble their circadian timing without touching their sleep or rest time. Related work found the same dim night worsened weight gain, glucose control and inflammation in animals on a high-fat diet. Sleep, metabolism and immunity seem to act as gears in a clock: if there’s one misalignment, the whole system is disrupted.
paras.zh: 在我的实验室里，我们在晚上饲养老鼠，灯光设置为 5 勒克斯，大约相当于孩子卧室夜灯的亮度。它们比在真正的黑暗中睡觉的老鼠体重增加了更多。他们并没有睡眠不足；夜光只是打乱了他们的生物钟基因节律，随后将他们的食物摄入转移到了一天中错误的时间。对于夜行性小鼠来说，它们将食物摄入量从夜间转移到白天。因为他们通常在白天睡觉，所以夜间的光线会扰乱他们的昼夜节律，而不会影响他们的睡眠或休息时间。相关研究发现，同样昏暗的夜晚会导致高脂肪饮食动物的体重增加、血糖控制和炎症恶化。睡眠、新陈代谢和免疫力似乎就像时钟中的齿轮：如果有一个失调，整个系统就会受到干扰。

paras.en: The obvious objection is fair: these are mice, they are nocturnal, they live in cages, and nobody has ever asked one how it slept. What happens when you run the experiment on people?
paras.zh: 明显的反对意见是公平的：这些是​​老鼠，它们是夜间活动的，它们住在笼子里，没有人问过它是如何睡觉的。当你对人进行实验时会发生什么？

paras.en: Researchers at Northwestern University put healthy young adults to bed for a single night in a room lit to 100 lux—dimmer than a well-lit kitchen, brighter than a night-light—and measured them in the morning. Their heart rates ran higher through the night. And by breakfast, they were measurably worse at handling sugar, assessed by increasing insulin resistance, than another group that slept in the dark.
paras.zh: 西北大学的研究人员让健康的年轻人在一个亮度为 100 勒克斯的房间里睡一晚——比光线充足的厨房更暗，比夜灯更亮——并在早上进行测量。他们的心率整夜都升高。通过胰岛素抵抗的增加来评估，到早餐时，他们处理糖分的能力明显比另一组在黑暗中睡觉的人差。

paras.en: That was one night in a laboratory, with 20 participants. “What happens over years in ordinary bedrooms?” is the harder question, and the best answer we have comes from 43,722 women, none of them shift workers, who were tracked for about five years. Those who slept with a television or a light on in the room were 17 percent more likely to gain 11 pounds or more and 33 percent more likely to develop obesity over that time, after researchers accounted for diet, exercise and sleep duration. Night-shift workers, who experience the extreme case of circadian rhythm disruption, carry higher rates of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, mood disorders and several cancers—though people who live that far out of phase with the sun differ from non-shift workers in many ways besides light.
paras.zh: 那是在实验室的一个晚上，有 20 名参与者。 “多年来，普通卧室里会发生什么？”这是一个更难的问题，我们的最佳答案来自 43,722 名女性，其中没有轮班工人，她们被跟踪了大约五年。研究人员考虑了饮食、锻炼和睡眠时间后，那些在房间里开着电视或灯睡觉的人在此期间体重增加 11 磅或以上的可能性增加了 17%，患肥胖症的可能性增加了 33%。夜班工人的昼夜节律受到严重破坏，他们患 2 型糖尿病、心血管疾病、情绪障碍和多种癌症的几率较高，尽管生活在与太阳的相位相差如此远的人与不值班工人在许多方面都存在差异，除了光线之外。

paras.en: The prescription costs almost nothing. Within an hour of waking, get outside for 10 to 30 minutes in whatever the sky is offering—an overcast morning outdoors still runs to thousands of lux; a well-lit kitchen only manages a few hundred. Sit near a window if you have one. In one small study, office workers with windows got far more daytime light than colleagues without them and slept the better part of an hour longer at night. When indoors in the evening, dim the lights and use warm light bulbs rather than overhead and blue lighting.
paras.zh: 处方几乎不需要花费任何费用。醒来一小时内，无论天气如何，到户外活动 10 到 30 分钟——阴天的早晨，户外的光照强度仍可达数千勒克斯；一个光线充足的厨房只能容纳几百人。如果有窗户的话，请坐在靠近窗户的地方。在一项小型研究中，有窗户的上班族比没有窗户的同事白天获得的光线要多得多，晚上的睡眠时间也多了一个小时。晚上在室内时，调暗灯光并使用暖色灯泡，而不是头顶和蓝色灯光。

paras.en: Then deal with the bedroom, which is the part everyone skips. Stand in yours tonight with the lights off and count what still glows: the router, the smoke detector, the charger, the standby light on the television, the sliver where the curtains refuse to meet.
paras.zh: 然后处理卧室，这是每个人都跳过的部分。今晚关掉灯，站在你家里，数数还有哪些东西还在发光：路由器、烟雾探测器、充电器、电视上的待机灯、窗帘无法接合的条子。

paras.en: Nobody is ever going to sell you a dark night. You will have to make it on your own.
paras.zh: 没有人会卖给你一个漆黑的夜晚。你必须自己做。

articles.title: These tattoos can magically' disappear—here’s how they work

paras.en: How handy would it be if you could make your tattoos invisible for a job interview in the morning, and reveal them again for a party in the evening? This sounds like science fiction, but it may soon be reality.
paras.zh: 如果你可以在早上面试时隐藏纹身，并在晚上参加聚会时再次露出纹身，那该有多方便？这听起来像是科幻小说，但它可能很快就会成为现实。

paras.en: Researchers at the University of Colorado Boulder have developed invisible tattoo ink than can be revealed with a UV torch and stays visible until switched off with white light. They have published their research in the journal Matter & Light.
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的研究人员开发出了隐形纹身墨水，可以用紫外线手电筒显示出来，并且在用白光关闭之前保持可见。他们在《物质与光》杂志上发表了他们的研究成果。

paras.en: They created different motifs with this ink ranging from a lantern that reveals its light when activated, to multicolored scales like those in the much-loved children’s book The Rainbow Fish.
paras.zh: 他们用这种墨水创造了不同的图案，从启动时发出光芒的灯笼，到深受喜爱的儿童读物《彩虹鱼》中的五彩鳞片。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The pigments used in these inks are so-called photochromic dyes(from the Greek “photos”, which means “light” and “chroma”, which means “color”). In other words, they are compounds that change colour when exposed to light. These dyes have been used for years in color-changing sunglasses.
paras.zh: 这些墨水中使用的颜料是所谓的光致变色染料（来自希腊语“photos”，意思是“光”和“chroma”，意思是“颜色”）。换句话说，它们是暴露在光线下会变色的化合物。这些染料多年来一直用于变色太阳镜。

paras.en: Light carries energy, and photochromic compounds are designed in such a way that this energy is enough to cause a chemical change that alters the shape and therefore the properties of the molecule.
paras.zh: 光携带能量，光致变色化合物的设计方式使得这种能量足以引起化学变化，从而改变分子的形状，从而改变分子的特性。

paras.en: In the case of the “invisible” tattoo ink, two or three seconds of bright ultraviolet (UV) light is enough to form a new ring in the dye molecule, which switches a colorless pigment to a colored one. A variety of colors are available depending on the exact structure of the molecule.
paras.zh: 对于“隐形”纹身墨水，两到三秒的明亮紫外线（UV）光足以在染料分子中形成一个新的环，将无色颜料转变为有色颜料。根据分子的具体结构，有多种颜色可供选择。

paras.en: A blast of bright white light reverses the reaction, breaking the ring and turning the colour off again. For a long time, the challenge with this chemistry was that the colored form of the dye was relatively unstable and quickly reverted to the more stable, colorless form—especially at higher temperatures.
paras.zh: 一阵明亮的白光逆转了反应，打破了环并再次关闭了颜色。长期以来，这种化学方法面临的挑战是染料的有色形式相对不稳定，并且很快会恢复到更稳定的无色形式，尤其是在较高温度下。

paras.en: Another issue was fatigue: after a certain number of on-off cycles, the dyes degraded and took on a permanent coloured hue. Have you ever bought transition lens sunglasses and noticed that they became less effective over time? This is due to the same deterioration of photochromic compounds in the lenses. But thanks to recent research efforts, remarkably stable dyes have been designed that reliably hold their colour for months and can undergo over 10,000 activation and deactivation cycles without degrading.
paras.zh: 另一个问题是疲劳：经过一定次数的开关循环后，染料会降解并呈现永久性的色调。您是否曾经购买过过渡镜片太阳镜，却发现随着时间的推移，它们的效果会变得越来越差？这是由于镜片中的光致变色化合物同样劣化所致。但得益于最近的研究工作，我们设计出了非常稳定的染料，可以可靠地保持其颜色数月，并且可以经历 10,000 多次激活和失活循环而不会降解。

paras.en: Carson Bruns’ team at the University of Colorado Boulder showed that these pigments could be formulated into tattoo inks by encapsulating them in poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), a polymer approved for medical use in bone cement, dentures and intraocular lenses. This family of inks is known as PhotoTat.
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的 Carson Bruns 团队表明，通过将这些颜料封装在聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯 (PMMA) 中，可以将其配制为纹身墨水，聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯是一种被批准用于骨水泥、假牙和人工晶状体医疗用途的聚合物。该系列墨水称为 PhotoTat。

paras.en: So, when will you be able to get one of these switchable tattoos? A red pigment was already launched in 2024 under the name Magic Ink by Colorado-based biotech company Hyprskn. A 2 millilitre (ml) vial will set you back £77, which is about 100 times more expensive than regular tattoo ink due to the specialised dyes and formulation process required. The ink is fully compliant with the EU’s Reach (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals) safety regulations.
paras.zh: 那么，您什么时候才能获得这些可切换纹身之一呢？总部位于科罗拉多州的生物技术公司 Hyprskn 已于 2024 年推出了一种名为 Magic Ink 的红色颜料。一瓶 2 毫升 (ml) 的纹身墨水售价为 77 英镑，由于需要专门的染料和配方工艺，这比普通纹身墨水贵约 100 倍。该墨水完全符合欧盟的 Reach（化学品注册、评估、授权和限制）安全法规。

paras.en: Now, Bruns’ research team has developed three more PhotoTat inks – blue, magenta and yellow – that can combine into 16 other colours. “So far,” Bruns says, “the only person who’s tested this ink is me. I actually have hundreds of these tattoos on my legs now and they’ve all gone really well.”
paras.zh: 现在，Bruns 的研究团队又开发了三种 PhotoTat 墨水——蓝色、品红色和黄色——可以组合成其他 16 种颜色。 “到目前为止，”布伦斯说，“唯一测试过这种墨水的人是我。事实上，我的腿上现在有数百个这样的纹身，而且都进展得很好。”

paras.en: Some challenges remain though: direct sunlight contains enough UV radiation to activate the tattoos unless they are protected by sunscreen. Indoor light will slowly switch them off over a period of several days.
paras.zh: 但仍然存在一些挑战：直射阳光含有足够的紫外线辐射来激活纹身，除非它们受到防晒霜的保护。室内灯光会在几天内慢慢关闭它们。

paras.en: In addition, the blue ink currently degrades after only 10–100 activations, leaving a permanent, purple-coloured mark. Most importantly, the inks need to undergo thorough toxicity and safety testing before they can be rolled out to tattoo shops for general use, which will likely take several years. Don’t get your hopes up just yet about your new “business during the day, party at night” look.
paras.zh: 此外，目前蓝色墨水仅在 10-100 次激活后就会降解，留下永久的紫色标记。最重要的是，这些墨水需要经过彻底的毒性和安全测试，然后才能推广到纹身店供一般使用，这可能需要几年的时间。不要对“白天工作，晚上聚会”的新造型抱有希望。

paras.en: When Hyprskn launched Magic Ink, the reception in the tattoo community was mixed. While some tattoo enthusiasts viewed it as a revolutionary creative tool, others thought it was an overpriced gimmick. Bruns does not only see his photochromic tattoo inks as fashion accessories, however.
paras.zh: 当 Hyprskn 推出 Magic Ink 时，纹身界的反响褒贬不一。虽然一些纹身爱好者将其视为一种革命性的创意工具，但其他人则认为这是一个价格过高的噱头。然而，布伦斯不仅将他的光致变色纹身墨水视为时尚配饰。

paras.en: He also envisages medical applications, for example for patients who need permanent skin markings to guide radiation therapy or identify sites for biopsies. Bruns argues that these markings “become a permanent reminder of a traumatic experience” which can be mitigated by making the tattoo invisible once it is no longer needed in a clinical setting.
paras.zh: 他还设想了医疗应用，例如对于需要永久性皮肤标记来指导放射治疗或识别活检部位的患者。布伦斯认为，这些标记“成为对创伤经历的永久提醒”，一旦临床环境中不再需要纹身，可以通过将纹身隐形来减轻这种情况。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: NASA’s Swift telescope will face a fiery demise after a failed rescue
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: For two decades, when the high-energy universe called, NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory has answered. But now, the spacecraft’s science tenure is ending, just when its skills might be more valuable than ever. The Swift spacecraft is falling uncontrollably, destined to burn up in Earth’s atmosphere in just a few days.
paras.zh: 二十年来，当高能宇宙发出召唤时，美国宇航局尼尔·格尔尔斯·斯威夫特天文台就会做出回应。但现在，航天器的科学任期即将结束，而此时它的技能可能比以往任何时候都更有价值。雨燕号宇宙飞船正在失控地坠落，几天之内注定会在地球大气层中燃烧殆尽。

paras.en: The telescope launched in 2004, tailored to reveal the secrets of gamma-ray bursts. These outbursts are the most powerful kind scientists have ever seen, but they often faded before earlier telescopes could respond. Swift took its name from its ability to jump to work when a flash went off. That talent both illuminated these elusive bursts and made the observatory a cornerstone of modern astronomy for far longer than scientists ever dreamed.
paras.zh: 该望远镜于 2004 年发射，专为揭示伽马射线暴的秘密而定制。这些爆发是科学家所见过的最强大的爆发，但它们常常在早期望远镜做出反应之前就消失了。 Swift 因其能够在闪光灯一亮时立即开始工作而得名。这种天赋不仅照亮了这些难以捉摸的爆发，也使该天文台成为现代天文学的基石，时间比科学家们想象的要长得多。

paras.en: “This was designed to be a two-year mission,” says astrophysicist Brad Cenko of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md. “We’re coming up on year 22. We are so fortunate to have had the opportunity to do all the things that we have.”
paras.zh: 马里兰州格林贝尔特美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心的天体物理学家 Brad Cenko 表示：“这是一项为期两年的任务。我们即将迎来第 22 年。我们很幸运有机会做我们拥有的所有事情。”

paras.en: Over the decades, the spacecraft has lost about half its original altitude as it constantly slammed into molecules in the atmosphere. Those minuscule impacts infinitesimally slowed the observatory, pushing it closer to Earth. The sun’s relatively high activity in recent years has accelerated the process, leaving the spacecraft unable to continue into the 2030s as engineers hoped. A spacecraft commissioned by NASA to loft Swift out of danger launched in early July, but by late August, technical issues made a boost attempt impossible.
paras.zh: 几十年来，由于不断撞击大气中的分子，航天器已经失去了大约一半的原始高度。这些微小的影响极大地减慢了天文台的速度，使其更接近地球。近年来太阳相对较高的活动加速了这一过程，导致航天器无法像工程师希望的那样持续到 2030 年代。美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 委托一艘航天器将雨燕号送出危险，该航天器于 7 月初发射升空，但到了 8 月底，技术问题使得助推尝试变得不可能。

paras.en: Swift is doomed — with nothing lined up to replace its unique capabilities.
paras.zh: Swift 注定要失败——没有任何东西可以取代它独特的功能。

paras.en: When scientists dreamed up the Swift mission, the massive energy and elusive nature of gamma-ray bursts made them one of the most tantalizing phenomena out there. Astronomers desperately wanted to understand how they worked.
paras.zh: 当科学家们梦想着雨燕号任务时，伽马射线暴的巨大能量和难以捉摸的性质使它们成为最诱人的现象之一。天文学家迫切想了解它们是如何工作的。

paras.en: Swift was equipped with three instruments. Its Burst Alert Telescope gave scientists eyes on gamma-ray emissions from up to half the visible sky, with the resolution to pinpoint where light is coming from. The agile spacecraft could then swing itself and its other instruments — one tuned to X-rays and the other to visible and ultraviolet light — to quickly give scientists a view of a patch of sky across a swath of types of light. It was a combination unlike any observatory before or since.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特配备了三种乐器。它的爆发警报望远镜让科学家们能够观察到半个可见天空的伽马射线发射，并能够精确定位光线的来源。然后，这艘敏捷的航天器可以摆动自身和其他仪器——一个调整到X射线，另一个调整到可见光和紫外光——以快速让科学家们看到一片天空中穿过一系列光的情况。这是一个不同于之前或之后任何天文台的组合。

paras.en: “It’s such a unique telescope,” says astrophysicist Wen-fai Fong of Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill., who is not part of the mission team. “It has all these views of the universe, all in one observatory, which by itself is rare, but it can also rapidly point any of these instruments.”
paras.zh: “这是一台非常独特的望远镜，”伊利诺伊州埃文斯顿西北大学的天体物理学家方文辉说道，他不是任务团队的成员。 “它拥有所有这些宇宙视图，全部集中在一个天文台中，这本身就很罕见，但它也可以快速指向任何这些仪器。”

paras.en: Swift’s roster of accomplishments speaks to the power of that recipe. “Almost immediately after launch, Swift started discovering things,” says astrophysicist Lynn Cominsky of Sonoma State University in Rohnert Park, Calif. That’s not an exaggeration: One record-breaking observation, taken just the month after launch, revealed that stellar corpses with powerful magnetic fields undergo outbursts that create a distinct kind of gamma-ray signature.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特的成就证明了这个秘诀的力量。加利福尼亚州罗内特公园索诺玛州立大学的天体物理学家林恩·科明斯基说：“几乎在发射后不久，斯威夫特就开始发现一些东西。”这并不夸张：发射后一个月进行的一项破纪录的观测表明，具有强大磁场的恒星尸体会发生爆发，从而产生一种独特的伽马射线特征。

paras.en: That observation pushed back against scientists’ existing categorization of gamma-ray bursts. Before Swift, the bursts fell into two buckets. Long gamma-ray bursts lasted as long as minutes, and scientists believed they stemmed from exploding stars triggering supernovae. Short gamma-ray bursts, in contrast, lasted less than two seconds and were believed to originate in merging neutron stars, the superdense remains of a star large enough to explode but too small to create a black hole.
paras.zh: 这一观察结果推翻了科学家现有的伽马射线暴分类。在斯威夫特之前，爆发分为两桶。长伽马射线爆发持续长达几分钟，科学家认为它们源于恒星爆炸引发的超新星。相比之下，短伽马射线暴持续时间不到两秒，被认为起源于中子星合并，中子星是一颗大到足以爆炸但又太小而无法形成黑洞的恒星的超致密残骸。

paras.en: Swift confirmed this basic sketch, but also complicated it by finding bursts that didn’t cleanly fit into this binary. “The more data you get, the more confused you get,” Cominsky says. Other notable bursts the telescope observed included the brightest (gamma-ray burst) of all time, nicknamed BOAT, the highest-energy photons from such a burst, and multiple claimants to the title of most distant burst.
paras.zh: 斯威夫特证实了这个基本的草图，但也通过发现不完全适合这个二进制文件的爆发来使其复杂化。 “你获得的数据越多，你就越困惑，”科明斯基说。该望远镜观测到的其他值得注意的爆发包括有史以来最亮的爆发（伽马射线暴），绰号为“船”，这种爆发中产生的最高能量光子，以及多个最遥远爆发称号的获得者。

paras.en: Notably, all of Swift’s data was public right away, even as team scientists were still working to understand what the telescope had seen. “That was very new,” Fong says, crediting the mission with inspiring other observatory teams to follow suit.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，斯威夫特的所有数据都立即公开，尽管团队科学家仍在努力了解望远镜所看到的内容。 “这是非常新的，”方说，并称赞这次任务激励了其他天文台团队效仿。

paras.en: As other astronomers heard about Swift’s work, they realized how powerful the observatory might be for their own interests as well. As Swift’s tenure unfolded, astronomers started asking to borrow the nimble observatory to study a whole range of objects changing on the sky.
paras.zh: 当其他天文学家听说斯威夫特的工作时，他们意识到天文台对于他们自己的利益也可能有多么强大。随着斯威夫特任期的展开，天文学家开始要求借用灵活的天文台来研究天空中变化的各种物体。

paras.en: “With scientists, if you give them a tool to do something, they will other find other things that you can do with that tool,” says astrophysicist Phil Evans of the University of Leicester in England. In its later years, Swift observed between five and 10 “targets of opportunity” most days, tallying hundreds or even thousands in a year.
paras.zh: 英国莱斯特大学的天体物理学家菲尔·埃文斯说：“对于科学家来说，如果你给他们一个工具来做某事，他们就会找到你可以用该工具做的其他事情。”在其晚年，斯威夫特大多数时候都会观察到 5 到 10 个“机会目标”，一年内会观察到数百甚至数千个。

paras.en: Perhaps its most ground-breaking collaborations were partnerships with observatories hunting for ghostly neutrinos that travel nearly as quickly as light but don’t interact often, and for gravitational waves, the ripples in spacetime triggered by massive objects. In 2017, Swift participated in back-to-back discoveries: the unique explosion caused by two neutron stars merging, then the first neutrino traced back to its origin.
paras.zh: 也许它最具突破性的合作是与天文台的合作，寻找幽灵般的中微子，它们的传播速度几乎与光一样快，但不经常相互作用，以及引力波，即由大质量物体引发的时空涟漪。 2017年，斯威夫特参与了背靠背的发现：两颗中子星合并引起的独特爆炸，然后第一个中微子追溯到它的起源。

paras.en: Since then, all efforts to observe light affiliated with a neutrino or gravitational-wave signal have come up empty. “We had these two really close together and then nothing since,” Evans says. “Which is frustrating, but also kind of fun.”
paras.zh: 从那时起，所有观测与中微子或引力波信号有关的光的努力都徒劳无功。埃文斯说：“我们两个人的关系非常密切，但从那以后就再也没有发生过。” “这令人沮丧，但也很有趣。”

paras.en: A range of current and future observatories will be able to take over some of Swift’s work, but not all of it. Even during the six months this year when Swift paused operations to prepare for the boost attempt, scientists felt its loss, says astrophysicist Judith Racusin of NASA Goddard. Racusin worked with Swift during its early years before turning her focus to NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, which launched in 2008 but boasts different strengths than its colleague. “We’re going to miss out,” she says of Swift’s loss. “Not just on the common events we have thousands of, but the really rare, unusual ones, which are often the ones we learn the most from.”
paras.zh: 当前和未来的一系列天文台将能够接管斯威夫特的部分工作，但不是全部。美国宇航局戈达德中心的天体物理学家朱迪思·拉库辛表示，即使在今年斯威夫特号暂停运行以准备助推尝试的六个月里，科学家们也感受到了损失。拉库辛早年曾与 Swift 合作，后来将重点转向美国宇航局的费米伽马射线太空望远镜，该望远镜于 2008 年发射，但拥有与其同事不同的优势。 “我们会错过的，”她谈到斯威夫特的损失时说道。 “不仅是我们有数以千计的常见事件，而且还有真正罕见、不寻常的事件，这些事件往往是我们学到最多的事件。”

paras.en: Mission personnel had Swift cram in as much science as possible as its demise approached. After the boost attempt was called off, the team turned Swift’s instruments back on for a scientific swan song. That included technical observations to ensure the utility of all its recent data, as well as indirect observations of Earth’s atmosphere at lower altitudes than many spacecraft are able to withstand. Swift even caught glimpses of a comet in its final weeks.
paras.zh: 在斯威夫特快要灭亡的时候，任务人员让斯威夫特灌输了尽可能多的科学知识。升压尝试被取消后，团队重新打开斯威夫特的仪器，谱写了一首科学的绝唱。其中包括确保其所有最新数据的实用性的技术观测，以及在比许多航天器能够承受的海拔更低的高度对地球大气层进行间接观测。斯威夫特甚至在最后几周瞥见了一颗彗星。

paras.en: And, of course, there were gamma-ray bursts. One particularly intriguing burst came in late September and was rather far away but remarkably energetic.
paras.zh: 当然，还有伽马射线爆发。九月下旬发生了一次特别有趣的爆发，虽然距离相当远，但能量却非常大。

paras.en: “It feels a little bit like a last hurrah of Swift,” Racusin says of the event. “It’s a burst that we’ll be studying for some time, so I’m really glad we got Swift data on it while we could.”
paras.zh: “这感觉有点像斯威夫特的最后一次欢呼，”拉库辛谈到这次活动时说道。 “这是一个我们将研究一段时间的爆发，所以我真的很高兴我们能够尽可能地获得有关它的 Swift 数据。”

articles.title: ‘Exhumed’ recounts the true story of America’s first vampire
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: October is my favorite month. I love when the leaves change colors and the air gets brisk. My hunger for media that sends a shiver down my spine is at an all-time high. This spooky season, I found satiation in Exhumed, a new book by historian Aaron Mahnke.
paras.zh: 十月是我最喜欢的月份。我喜欢树叶变色、空气清新的感觉。我对媒体的渴望达到了历史最高点，这让我脊背发凉。在这个令人毛骨悚然的季节，我在历史学家亚伦·马恩克（Aaron Mahnke）的新书《挖掘》（Exhumed）中找到了满足。

paras.en: Mahnke draws on rich science-based history and folklore to show how fear of the unknown has shaped culture throughout history, even into the present day. He cites Taylor Swift, Twilight and other pop culture phenomena in his analysis — a choice that injects fresh air into the otherwise miasmic atmosphere. And thanks to Mahnke’s gripping prose, I felt like I was in the middle of the action. It was hard to lay the book down.
paras.zh: 马恩克利用丰富的基于科学的历史和民间传说来展示对未知的恐惧如何在整个历史中塑造文化，甚至到了今天。他在分析中引用了泰勒·斯威夫特、《暮光之城》和其他流行文化现象——这一选择为原本瘴气的气氛注入了新鲜空气。感谢马恩克扣人心弦的散文，我感觉自己仿佛置身于故事之中。很难放下书。

paras.en: Exhumed kicks off with the true story of America’s first “vampire.”
paras.zh: 《挖掘》以美国第一个“吸血鬼”的真实故事开始。

paras.en: Walk with me for a moment back in time to Exeter, Rhode Island in 1892. Rampant tuberculosis is killing scores of people, including three members of the Brown family: matriarch Mary and her daughters, Mary O. and Mercy L. Then a son, Edwin, falls ill with the same symptoms — sparking concern that one of the women is an undead vampire who is sucking his life away. The town exhumes the bodies.
paras.zh: 和我一起回到 1892 年罗德岛州埃克塞特。猖獗的结核病正在夺去数十人的生命，其中包括布朗家族的三名成员：女族长玛丽和她的女儿玛丽·O. 和梅西·L。然后，一个儿子埃德温也出现了同样的症状，引发了人们的担忧，其中一名妇女是一个正在吸走他生命的不死吸血鬼。镇上挖出了尸体。

paras.en: Mercy is surprisingly well-preserved. Her hair and nails appear longer and blood dribbles from her skin when it is pierced, “evidence” that confirms everyone’s worst fear: Mercy is indeed a vampire. (Nevermind that she perished in the dead of winter, when temperatures were probably cold enough to substantially slow decomposition.) The town burns Mercy’s heart, though it doesn’t save poor Edwin. These events helped inspire Bram Stoker’s Dracula, which was published five years later.
paras.zh: 令人惊奇的是，慈悲保存完好。她的头发和指甲显得更长，当皮肤被刺穿时，血液会从她的皮肤上滴下来，“证据”证实了每个人最担心的事情：梅西确实是一个吸血鬼。 （别介意她是在隆冬时节死去的，当时的气温可能足够冷，可以大大减缓分解速度。）这座小镇灼伤了梅西的心，尽管它并没有拯救可怜的埃德温。这些事件激发了布拉姆·斯托克的《德古拉》的灵感，该书于五年后出版。

paras.en: Interestingly, the cause of tuberculosis — a bacterium — was discovered a full decade before Mercy’s story unfolded. But news doesn’t always travel fast and entrenched beliefs can be difficult to change, even in the face of hard evidence. Exhumed explores this idea far beyond Mercy’s tragic tale.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，结核病的病因——一种细菌——在梅西的故事展开之前整整十年就被发现了。但消息并不总是传播得很快，即使面对确凿的证据，根深蒂固的信念也很难改变。 《挖掘》对这个想法的探索远远超出了梅西的悲剧故事。

paras.en: Fear has led people to do some extremely odd things by today’s standards: burning hearts to kill “vampires,” setting boobie-traps in graves to prevent the dead from rising or drinking the blood of freshly hanged men to “cure” epilepsy. Without modern science to explain the unexplained, people often filled in the blanks with stories, Mahnke explains.
paras.zh: 恐惧导致人们做出一些以今天的标准来看极其奇怪的事情：焚烧心脏来杀死“吸血鬼”，在坟墓中设置陷阱以防止死者复活，或者喝刚上吊的人的血来“治愈”癫痫。马恩克解释说，由于没有现代科学来解释无法解释的事情，人们常常用故事来填补空白。

paras.en: He implores readers to withhold judgement. After all, storytelling is one of the main ways that humans make sense of the world. “All of us, both then and now, are simply making the best of what we have, trying to find a way to improve our lives,” Mahnke writes.
paras.zh: 他恳请读者不要做出判断。毕竟，讲故事是人类理解世界的主要方式之一。 “我们所有人，无论是过去还是现在，都只是在充分利用我们所拥有的一切，试图找到一种方法来改善我们的生活，”马恩克写道。

paras.en: Perhaps this practice continues today in different shades.
paras.zh: 也许这种做法今天仍在以不同的方式延续着。

paras.en: At one point, eating mummies, or “mumia,” was considered cure-all for most ailments —headaches, stomach troubles and general sickness. Is it too far from the expectations some people have of buying a “health shot” from Whole Foods? Not really!
paras.zh: 曾几何时，吃木乃伊或“mumia”被认为能治愈大多数疾病——头痛、胃病和一般疾病。这与一些人从全食超市购买“健康疫苗”的期望相去甚远吗？并不真地！

paras.en: More than a century after Mercy Brown’s heart was incinerated, we’re still clinging to stories and rituals that offer us a sense of control over the thing we fear most: death. Exhumed makes it clear that we haven’t outrun this instinct, we’ve just given it different packaging.
paras.zh: 梅西·布朗的心脏被焚毁一个多世纪后，我们仍然坚持相信故事和仪式，这些故事和仪式让我们有一种控制我们最害怕的事情的感觉：死亡。 《挖掘》清楚地表明，我们并没有超越这种本能，我们只是给了它不同的包装。

paras.en: If you are the type of person who has 50 tabs open at any given moment, then you will appreciate Exhumed’s myriad quirky facts. Here are three of my favorites:
paras.zh: 如果您是那种在任何特定时刻都会打开 50 个标签的人，那么您将会欣赏《Exhumed》中无数离奇的事实。以下是我最喜欢的三个：

paras.en: - Leonardo da Vinci was a fan of corpse medicine, the practice of reusing body parts from dead people for medicinal purposes. Like many of his peers, da Vinci believed the human body contained “vital spirits.” When someone died, there’d be leftover spirits for the living to make use of.
paras.zh: - 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是尸体医学的爱好者，即重新利用死者的身体部位用于医疗目的。和许多同龄人一样，达·芬奇相信人体含有“生命力”。人死后，会有剩余的灵魂供生者使用。

paras.en: - In 17th century Europe, the tomato was known as the “poison apple.” Many people became sick after eating tomatoes and some even died. For two centuries, society wrongly blamed the fruit. The real killer turned out to be lead leached out of pewter dishes by tomatoes’ acidic juice.
paras.zh: - 在 17 世纪的欧洲，番茄被称为“毒苹果”。很多人吃了西红柿就生病了，有的甚至死亡。两个世纪以来，社会错误地指责这种水果。事实证明，真正的杀手是番茄酸性汁从锡盘中浸出的铅。

paras.en: - The spinning red, white and blue poles on barbershops were born out of the business’ former specialty, bloodletting. Red stripes stand for blood, blue for veins and white for the rags used for clean-up. The ball on top is said to represent the bowl that captured the blood. And the pole itself represents the wand patients squeezed during the procedure. Feeling sick in 1705? Head to the local barber with the spinning pole outside.
paras.zh: - 理发店里旋转的红、白、蓝柱子源于该行业以前的专业——放血。红色条纹代表血液，蓝色条纹代表静脉，白色条纹代表清洁用的抹布。据说顶部的球代表盛有血液的碗。杆子本身代表手术过程中患者被挤压的魔杖。 1705 年感觉不舒服吗？前往当地理发店，理发店外面有旋转杆。

paras.en: Buy Exhumed from Bookshop.org. Science News is a Bookshop.org affiliate and will earn a commission on purchases made from links in this article.
paras.zh: 从 Bookshop.org 购买《Exhumed》。 《科学新闻》是 Bookshop.org 的附属机构，通过本文中的链接进行购买将赚取佣金。

articles.title: This Halloween, amateur astronomers may be in for a dwarf planet treat
articles.author: Lisa Grossman

paras.en: The outer solar system is yielding its secrets to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory.
paras.zh: 外太阳系正在向维拉·C·鲁宾天文台透露其秘密。

paras.en: Less than five months into the observatory’s decade-long survey of the sky, a potential new dwarf planet has already popped up in its data, astronomers reported this week at a meeting of the American Astronomical Society’s Division of Planetary Sciences in Spokane, Wash.
paras.zh: 天文学家本周在华盛顿州斯波坎举行的美国天文学会行星科学部会议上报告说，天文台对天空进行了长达十年的调查不到五个月，一颗潜在的新矮行星已经出现在其数据中。

paras.en: Another team reported a handful of new Neptune Trojans, icy objects that share an orbit with Neptune, at the meeting and in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. The findings are filling in astronomers’ picture of the Kuiper Belt at the solar system’s frigid fringes.
paras.zh: 另一个团队在会议上和《天体物理学杂志快报》上报告了一些新的海王星特洛伊木马，它们是与海王星共享轨道的冰冷物体。这些发现填补了天文学家对太阳系寒冷边缘柯伊伯带的想象。

paras.en: “It feels a little bit like we’re replicating the 1800s and early 1900s, discovering what the solar system even looks like in general,” says Sam Deen, an amateur astronomer based in Simi Valley, Calif. “We’re finding out what there even is in the first place that makes up most of the Kuiper Belt.”
paras.zh: 加利福尼亚州西米谷的业余天文学家萨姆·迪恩 (Sam Deen) 表示：“感觉有点像我们正在复制 1800 年代和 1900 年代初期，探索太阳系的总体面貌。我们正在寻找构成柯伊伯带大部分区域的物质。”

paras.en: A possible dwarf planet hid in historical data
paras.zh: 历史数据中隐藏着一颗可能的矮行星

paras.en: Perched on a mountaintop in Chile, the Vera Rubin Observatory is on a mission to map the entire southern sky every couple of nights, searching for faint and fast-moving cosmic objects. The observatory took its first images in June 2025 and officially began a decade-long survey in June 2026.
paras.zh: 维拉鲁宾天文台坐落在智利的山顶上，其任务是每隔几个晚上绘制整个南部天空的地图，寻找微弱且快速移动的宇宙物体。该天文台于 2025 年 6 月拍摄了第一张图像，并于 2026 年 6 月正式开始为期十年的调查。

paras.en: Even before the official survey started, Rubin had detected the motion of an object orbiting billions of kilometers beyond Pluto. Rubin observed the object 30 times on 20 nights from March 4 to July 11. But no one knew it was there until October 13, when astrophysicist Matt Holman of the Smithsonian Astronomical Observatory in Cambridge, Mass., ran a search for moving dots of light in the data.
paras.zh: 甚至在官方调查开始之前，鲁宾就探测到了一个绕冥王星数十亿公里运行的物体的运动。从3月4日到7月11日，鲁宾在20个晚上观察了这个物体30次。但直到10月13日，马萨诸塞州剑桥史密森天文台的天体物理学家马特·霍尔曼在数据中寻找移动的光点时，才有人知道它在那里。

paras.en: The object, called 2026 ED138, appeared to be about 47 times as far from Earth as Earth is from the sun. Its brightness suggests it’s between 600 and 1,500 kilometers wide, potentially as large as other dwarf planets like Ceres and Makemake. That’s probably big enough to be spherical, making it a dwarf planet.
paras.zh: 这个被称为 2026 ED138 的天体距离地球的距离似乎是地球距离太阳距离的 47 倍。它的亮度表明它的宽度在 600 到 1,500 公里之间，可能与谷神星和鸟神星等其他矮行星一样大。它可能足够大，成为球形，使其成为一颗矮行星。

paras.en: “It’s really big. It’s damn huge,” Deen says. “No matter what you call it, it’s still the biggest thing we’ve found in the entire solar system in 19 years.”
paras.zh: “它真的很大。真是太大了，”迪恩说。 “不管你怎么称呼它，它仍然是 19 年来我们在整个太阳系中发现的最大的东西。”

paras.en: When Holman realized what he had found, he was thrilled but doubtful. “It’s quite an exciting thing,” Holman said in a news briefing at the meeting on October 27. “But one of the things that you need to do when you discover something potentially of this size is to try to verify that it’s true.”
paras.zh: 当霍尔曼意识到他的发现时，他很兴奋，但也很怀疑。 “这是一件非常令人兴奋的事情，”霍尔曼在 10 月 27 日的会议新闻发布会上说。“但是，当你发现这种规模的潜在东西时，你需要做的事情之一就是尝试验证它的真实性。”

paras.en: Holman and colleagues were able to find observations of the same object in archived data from the Dark Energy Camera, located on an adjacent mountaintop in Chile, taken in 2016.
paras.zh: 霍尔曼和同事能够在 2016 年拍摄的位于智利邻近山顶的暗能量相机的存档数据中找到对同一物体的观察结果。

paras.en: Deen was able to trace it back even farther, to photographic plates taken as part of a sky survey at Palomar Observatory in California in 1954. Other amateur astronomers independently found the same sightings.
paras.zh: 迪恩能够追溯到更远的地方，追溯到 1954 年在加利福尼亚州帕洛玛天文台进行天空调查时拍摄的照片底片。其他业余天文学家独立发现了相同的目击事件。

paras.en: “They took an image from Palomar in 1954, and another about half an hour after the first one, that both by pure chance happen to point at where ED138 is,” Deen says. “And it’s really obvious. If you know it’s supposed to be there, it’s not particularly faint.”
paras.zh: “他们于 1954 年在帕洛玛拍摄了一张照片，在第一张照片拍摄后大约半小时又拍摄了一张照片，这两张照片都纯属偶然地指向了 ED138 所在的位置，”迪恩说。 “而且它真的很明显。如果你知道它应该在那里，它就不会特别微弱。”

paras.en: So why didn’t anybody notice it until now? It’s partly because ED138 practically crawls across the sky, orbiting the sun once every 280 years. It was also moving against a dense background of Milky Way stars, where it blended in.
paras.zh: 那么为什么直到现在还没有人注意到它呢？部分原因是 ED138 几乎在天空中爬行，每 280 年绕太阳一周。它也在密集的银河系恒星背景下移动，并融入其中。

paras.en: By combining observations spanning decades, astronomers can calculate the object’s orbit with more precision.
paras.zh: 通过结合数十年的观测结果，天文学家可以更精确地计算该物体的轨道。

paras.en: Deen is hoping to observe the potential new dwarf planet pass in front of a distant star on Halloween. That sort of observation, called an occultation, can help reveal more details of the putative dwarf planet’s size and shape, and even whether it has moons or rings. Usually, it takes years to understand an object’s orbit well enough to predict an occultation, Deen says. “Getting to do it immediately is like being a kid in a candy shop, really.”
paras.zh: 迪恩希望在万圣节观察到潜在的新矮行星从一颗遥远的恒星前面经过。这种被称为掩星的观察可以帮助揭示假定的矮行星的大小和形状的更多细节，甚至它是否有卫星或环。迪恩说，通常需要数年时间才能充分了解物体的轨道以预测掩星。 “立即开始做这件事就像是一个在糖果店里的孩子，真的。”

paras.en: Icy objects could offer clues to solar system beginnings
paras.zh: 冰冷的物体可以为太阳系的起源提供线索

paras.en: A crop of newly spotted Neptune Trojans were masked by the Milky Way, too. These asteroids gather in the same orbit as Neptune, but offset from the planet at 60 degrees. Astronomers think they were some of the original building blocks of the solar system and contain an ancient record of planetary formation and evolution.
paras.zh: 一批新发现的海王星特洛伊人也被银河系掩盖了。这些小行星聚集在与海王星相同的轨道上，但与海王星的偏移角度为 60 度。天文学家认为它们是太阳系的一些原始组成部分，并且包含行星形成和演化的古老记录。

paras.en: Other planets have Trojans, too. Jupiter has thousands. Astronomers think Neptune has many more, but so far they have seen only 30 in the cluster of space objects that orbit ahead of Neptune, and just two in the cluster behind it.
paras.zh: 其他行星也有特洛伊人。木星有数千个。天文学家认为海王星还有更多，但到目前为止，他们在海王星前面的空间物体星团中只看到了 30 个，而在海王星后面的星团中只看到了 2 个。

paras.en: “We would expect these [groups of Trojans] to be symmetric in numbers, so you have to get more than two,” planetary scientist Meg Schwamb said in a news conference at the meeting on October 28.
paras.zh: “我们预计这些[特洛伊木马群]在数量上是对称的，因此必须有两个以上，”行星科学家梅格·施万布 (Meg Schwamb) 在 10 月 28 日会议的新闻发布会上说道。

paras.en: The trailing cloud happened to have been moving in front of the Milky Way from the perspective of Earth for the last 15 years. Spotting individual Trojans against that crowded background was “like finding a needle in a sequined dress,” said Schwamb, of Queens University Belfast in Northern Ireland.
paras.zh: 在过去的 15 年里，从地球的角度来看，尾随云恰好一直在银河系前面移动。北爱尔兰贝尔法斯特女王大学的施万布说，在拥挤的背景下发现单个特洛伊木马“就像在亮片连衣裙中找到一根针”。

paras.en: Schwamb and colleagues examined Vera Rubin data taken from the commissioning phase — the period when engineers were testing the telescope. In this early data haul, the team found two more trailing Trojans, plus one candidate. They seem to be similar in composition to the leading ones, which matches theories of how the solar system formed.
paras.zh: 施万布和同事检查了维拉·鲁宾在调试阶段（工程师测试望远镜的时期）获取的数据。在早期的数据采集中，团队发现了另外两个跟踪特洛伊木马，以及一个候选木马。它们的组成似乎与主要的类似，这与太阳系形成的理论相匹配。

paras.en: “It just kind of got lucky,” Schwamb said. “These objects photobombed the commissioning survey.”
paras.zh: “这只是运气好，”施万布说。 “这些物体对调试调查进行了照片轰炸。”

paras.en: “This is really the appetizer for what Rubin Observatory is going to do in its mission for the next ten years,” she added. “There’s hundreds more of these objects likely to be found.”
paras.zh: “这确实是鲁宾天文台未来十年使命的开胃菜，”她补充道。 “可能还会发现数百个这样的物体。”

paras.en: Some of the excitement about these discoveries is dampened by fears of losing observations to bright satellites crisscrossing the telescope’s field of view, says astronomer Sam Lawler of the University of Regina in Canada.
paras.zh: 加拿大里贾纳大学的天文学家萨姆·劳勒说，这些发现的一些兴奋感因担心观测结果被穿过望远镜视场的明亮卫星而减弱。

paras.en: “I have to put in the constant downer of how the increasing numbers of satellites will make these discoveries harder,” Lawler says. “There are one hundred new satellites launching every week, and they keep getting bigger and brighter. These discoveries will be hindered by that.”
paras.zh: “我必须不断地沮丧，因为卫星数量的增加将使这些发现变得更加困难，”劳勒说。 “每周都有一百颗新卫星发射，而且它们变得越来越大、越来越亮。这些发现将因此受到阻碍。”

paras.en: But even with the satellites, Lawler anticipates many more cool discoveries from Rubin.
paras.zh: 但即使有了卫星，劳勒预计鲁宾还会有更多酷的发现。

paras.en: “Just finding a dwarf planet so quickly, maybe we’ll find something even bigger,” she says. “There could be something the size of Mars out there. And then we’d have the whole planet debate all over again. It would be fun.”
paras.zh: “这么快就找到了一颗矮行星，也许我们会发现更大的东西，”她说。 “那里可能有火星那么大的东西。然后我们会再次进行整个星球的辩论。这会很有趣。”

articles.title: Just 30 Minutes in a Sauna Triggers an Immediate Immune Response
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Some people swear by a sauna session. They claim that sitting and sweating in a hot room rejuvenates them.
paras.zh: 有些人非常喜欢桑拿。他们声称坐在炎热的房间里出汗可以让他们恢复活力。

paras.en: But for such a popular trend, the scientific evidence to support that feeling is surprisingly scarce.
paras.zh: 但对于如此流行的趋势，支持这种感觉的科学证据却出奇地稀少。

paras.en: Researchers in Finland have now found evidence that a single sauna session can have an immediate impact on the immune system at a cellular level.
paras.zh: 芬兰的研究人员现已发现证据表明，一次桑拿可以在细胞水平上对免疫系统产生立竿见影的影响。

paras.en: In a small experiment, just 30 minutes in a Finnish sauna – with hot yet dry heat – triggered a significant increase in circulating white blood cells.
paras.zh: 在一项小型实验中，在芬兰桑拿房（高温且干热）中呆上 30 分钟，就会引发循环白细胞的显着增加。

paras.en: These crucial immune cells help defend the body against pathogens, and they often increase after exercise.
paras.zh: 这些重要的免疫细胞有助于保护身体免受病原体侵害，并且它们通常会在运动后增加。

paras.en: Simply sitting in a sauna could stimulate a similar stress response, and it could have benefits for the immune system.
paras.zh: 简单地坐在桑拿房里就可以刺激类似的压力反应，并且对免疫系统有好处。

paras.en: The results are published in Temperature.
paras.zh: 结果发表在《温度》杂志上。

paras.en: "This may indicate that sauna bathing mobilizes additional white blood cells into the bloodstream from tissues, where they are then redeposited after the session," speculates exercise scientist Ilkka Heinonen from the University of Turku in Finland.
paras.zh: 芬兰图尔库大学的运动科学家伊尔卡·海诺宁 (Ilkka Heinonen) 推测：“这可能表明，桑拿浴会从组织中调动额外的白细胞进入血液，然后在沐浴后重新沉积在血液中。”

paras.en: "This kind of periodic release of white blood cells into the bloodstream is beneficial, as once they leave their storage sites, they are better able to patrol the body and respond to pathogens."
paras.zh: “这种白细胞定期释放到血液中的方式是有益的，因为一旦它们离开储存地点，它们就能够更好地巡逻身体并对病原体做出反应。”

paras.en: In the experiment, 51 middle-aged men and women took part in a traditional Finnish sauna session.
paras.zh: 在实验中，51名中年男女参加了传统的芬兰桑拿课程。

paras.en: This included sitting in a room at around 73° Celsius (163° Fahrenheit) for 30 minutes, with a cold shower halfway through.
paras.zh: 这包括在大约 73 摄氏度（163 华氏度）的房间里坐 30 分钟，中途洗冷水澡。

paras.en: Immediately after the session, a whole host of white blood cells appeared to be mobilized in the blood of participants compared to before the sauna session.
paras.zh: 与桑拿浴前相比，桑拿浴结束后，参与者的血液中似乎动员了大量的白细胞。

paras.en: This included an increase in neutrophils, which are first responders, and lymphocytes, which help build immune memory.
paras.zh: 这包括中性粒细胞（第一反应者）和淋巴细胞（有助于建立免疫记忆）的增加。

paras.en: There was also an increase in the combined count of monocytes, which engulf pathogens and debris, and eosinophils and basophils, which are both linked to inflammatory responses.
paras.zh: 单核细胞（吞噬病原体和碎片）以及嗜酸性粒细胞和嗜碱性粒细胞的组合计数也有所增加，这两者都与炎症反应有关。

paras.en: Levels of immune messenger proteins called cytokines, on the other hand, barely shifted, on average, although a few did increase with body temperature.
paras.zh: 另一方面，被称为细胞因子的免疫信使蛋白的水平平均而言几乎没有变化，尽管有一些确实随着体温的升高而增加。

paras.en: Thirty minutes after the sauna session, however, this apparent immune surge had mostly dropped off again.
paras.zh: 然而，桑拿浴三十分钟后，这种明显的免疫激增又大部分下降了。

paras.en: Most of the white blood cell increases had disappeared, but some monocytes lingered.
paras.zh: 大部分白细胞的增加已经消失，但一些单核细胞仍然存在。

paras.en: Researchers only analyzed participants' bloodwork up to 30 minutes after the sauna session, so it is unclear how their immune cells might change over longer periods of time or how that might impact their risk of getting sick.
paras.zh: 研究人员仅分析了参与者在桑拿后 30 分钟内的血液检查，因此尚不清楚他们的免疫细胞在较长时间内可能会发生怎样的变化，或者这可能会如何影响他们生病的风险。

paras.en: But some observational studies in the past have found that frequent sauna bathing is associated with a lower risk of some illnesses, like pneumonia.
paras.zh: 但过去的一些观察性研究发现，经常洗桑拿可以降低患肺炎等疾病的风险。

paras.en: What's more, other experiments have shown that hot baths can lower your blood pressure and significantly increase red blood cells that carry oxygen.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，其他实验表明，热水浴可以降低血压，并显着增加携带氧气的红细胞。

paras.en: Bathing in heat seems to produce similar physiological responses to what occurs during exercise, and these cardiovascular outcomes are linked to improved immune function.
paras.zh: 沐浴在高温中似乎会产生与运动时类似的生理反应，而这些心血管结果与免疫功能的改善有关。

paras.en: That said, vigorous exercise can also backfire, temporarily weakening the immune system, so there's reason to tread cautiously.
paras.zh: 也就是说，剧烈运动也会适得其反，暂时削弱免疫系统，所以有理由谨慎行事。

paras.en: Extreme heat isn't something to mess with.
paras.zh: 极端炎热并不是什么值得烦恼的事情。

paras.en: Despite growing global interest in hot and cold therapy, scientists still know remarkably little about how the body copes with extreme temperatures, and what that means for our short-term or long-term health.
paras.zh: 尽管全球对冷热疗法的兴趣日益浓厚，但科学家们对身体如何应对极端温度以及这对我们的短期或长期健康意味着什么仍然知之甚少。

paras.en: The recent experiment in Finland is limited in what it can tell us.
paras.zh: 最近在芬兰进行的实验所能告诉我们的信息有限。

paras.en: Researchers did not measure specific immune cell subsets, like T cells or natural killer cells, which could have provided more insight into how a sauna actually impacts immune function.
paras.zh: 研究人员没有测量特定的免疫细胞亚群，如 T 细胞或自然杀伤细胞，这可以让我们更深入地了解桑拿实际上如何影响免疫功能。

paras.en: In 2023, for instance, a study reported that Finnish sauna sessions altered T cells and natural killer cells, but only when the sessions were repeated.
paras.zh: 例如，2023 年的一项研究报告称，芬兰桑拿浴改变了 T 细胞和自然杀伤细胞，但仅限于重复进行桑拿浴时。

paras.en: What's more, the impact was different depending on whether the participants were trained sauna-goers or not.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，根据参与者是否接受过桑拿训练，影响也不同。

paras.en: In this experiment, repeated sauna exposure increased white blood cell counts in trained participants, but it reduced some T cells in untrained participants.
paras.zh: 在这个实验中，重复的桑拿浴增加了受过训练的参与者的白细胞计数，但它减少了未经训练的参与者的一些 T 细胞。

paras.en: That study, however, only analyzed healthy young men, which limits how these results can be generalized to others.
paras.zh: 然而，该研究仅分析了健康的年轻男性，这限制了将这些结果推广到其他人的方式。

paras.en: For now, all we can say is that it looks increasingly like bathing in heat can trigger a temporary change to immune cells.
paras.zh: 目前，我们只能说，沐浴在高温中似乎越来越能引发免疫细胞的暂时变化。

paras.en: Plus, it's good to remember that just like cold therapy, hot therapy might also come with risks…
paras.zh: 另外，最好记住，就像冷疗一样，热疗也可能带来风险……

paras.en: The research has been published in Temperature.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《温度》杂志上。

articles.title: Aphantasia: Some People Can't Picture Things While Awake, But See Them in Dreams
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Picture someone you know well. You might be able to bring their face to mind, perhaps their smile or the way their hair falls. For some people, that familiar face never becomes a mental picture, however hard they try.
paras.zh: 想象一个你很熟悉的人。你也许能够想起他们的脸，也许是他们的微笑或他们的头发掉落的方式。对于某些人来说，无论他们多么努力，那张熟悉的面孔永远不会成为脑海中的画面。

paras.en: When they fall asleep, this can change. Faces and places may appear in their dreams, even though they cannot deliberately picture them during the day.
paras.zh: 当他们入睡时，这种情况就会改变。面孔和地点可能会出现在他们的梦中，尽管他们在白天无法刻意描绘它们。

paras.en: What allows those images to appear during sleep?
paras.zh: 是什么让这些图像在睡眠时出现？

paras.en: The inability to picture things at will is known as aphantasia. A study published in Scientific Reports explored the dreams of people who have it and found that the relationship between waking imagination and dreaming varies considerably from person to person.
paras.zh: 无法随意想象事物被称为失语症。发表在《科学报告》上的一项研究探讨了做梦的人的梦境，发现清醒时的想象力和做梦之间的关系因人而异。

paras.en: The researchers looked beyond images, asking about sounds, smells, tastes, touch, the feeling of movement, and inner speech, the experience of hearing words in your mind.
paras.zh: 研究人员不仅关注图像，还询问声音、气味、味道、触觉、运动的感觉以及内心言语，即在脑海中听到单词的体验。

paras.en: Some people described similar sensory experiences while dreaming and imagining things awake. Others reported sensations in dreams that they could not deliberately summon during waking life.
paras.zh: 有些人在做梦和想象清醒时描述了类似的感官体验。其他人则报告说，梦中的感觉是他们在清醒生活中无法刻意唤起的。

paras.en: The question had a personal beginning. Two of the researchers, Derek Arnold and Loren Bouyer of the University of Queensland in Australia, describe having lifelong aphantasia. Their dreams are not alike, and each felt that the sensations in their dreams reflected those they could imagine during the day.
paras.zh: 这个问题有一个个人的开始。澳大利亚昆士兰大学的两名研究人员德里克·阿诺德（Derek Arnold）和洛伦·布耶（Loren Bouyer）描述了患有终生失语症的情况。他们的梦并不相似，每个人都觉得梦中的感觉反映了他们白天所能想象的感觉。

paras.en: They had previously described how their imaginations differ. Arnold can imagine sounds, while Bouyer can imagine sensations of touch. Neither can voluntarily form mental pictures.
paras.zh: 他们之前曾描述过他们的想象力有何不同。阿诺德可以想象声音，而布耶可以想象触觉。两者都不能自愿形成心理图像。

paras.en: Working with Merlin Monzel of the University of Bonn in Germany, they investigated how these experiences varied among a larger group.
paras.zh: 他们与德国波恩大学的梅林·蒙泽尔合作，研究了这些经历在较大群体中的差异。

paras.en: The team analyzed online questionnaire responses from 205 people. Scores measuring visual imagination placed 84 participants in a visual aphantasia group and 121 in a comparison group.
paras.zh: 该团队分析了 205 人的在线问卷调查回复。测量视觉想象力的分数将 84 名参与者划分为视觉失语症组，将 121 名参与者划分为对照组。

paras.en: Participants considered situations that might bring different senses to mind, such as remembering a social gathering. They ranked the imagined sensations they experienced and answered questions about everyday habits, including mentally rehearsing conversations or imagining how a movement would feel.
paras.zh: 参与者考虑了可能会带来不同感觉的情况，例如记得一次社交聚会。他们对所经历的想象感觉进行排序，并回答有关日常习惯的问题，包括在心里排练对话或想象某个动作的感觉。

paras.en: They also reported how often different sensations appeared in their dreams, with an option to say they were unsure.
paras.zh: 他们还报告了梦中出现不同感觉的频率，并可以选择表示不确定。

paras.en: Within the aphantasia group, 46 percent reported always having visual experiences in their dreams. About 8 percent reported never having them. Nobody in the comparison group reported experiencing visual dreams.
paras.zh: 在失语症组中，46% 的人表示在梦中总是有视觉体验。大约 8% 的人表示从未拥有过它们。对照组中没有人报告经历过视觉梦。

paras.en: Among participants in the aphantasia group, the researchers found no evidence that stronger waking visualization went along with more frequent visual dreaming.
paras.zh: 在失语症组的参与者中，研究人员发现没有证据表明更强的清醒想象与更频繁的视觉梦有关。

paras.en: The connections were clearer for sounds and inner speech. Participants who reported these experiences more often in dreams also tended to report them more often while awake, although the associations were generally weak to moderate.
paras.zh: 声音和内心言语的联系更加清晰。在梦中更频繁地报告这些经历的参与者也倾向于在清醒时更频繁地报告这些经历，尽管这种关联通常较弱到中等。

paras.en: People in the aphantasia group who often heard sounds and conversations while dreaming also tended to report more frequent use of imagined sounds and inner speech in daily life, such as mentally rehearsing conversations before speaking.
paras.zh: 失语症组中经常在做梦时听到声音和对话的人也倾向于在日常生活中更频繁地使用想象的声音和内心言语，例如在说话之前在心里排练对话。

paras.en: Across the three questionnaires, participants were consistent in how closely their waking imagination matched their dreams. Some repeatedly reported a close match, while others described substantial differences.
paras.zh: 在三份问卷中，参与者在清醒时的想象力与梦境的匹配程度方面是一致的。一些人反复报告了一场势均力敌的比赛，而另一些人则描述了巨大的差异。

paras.en: Why a sensation would be available during sleep but not on demand while awake is still unclear. One possible explanation involves how brain regions involved in imagination work together. The researchers suggest that difficulties coordinating this activity might continue during sleep for some people, while changing for others.
paras.zh: 为什么在睡眠时会有感觉，但在清醒时却不能按需感觉，目前尚不清楚。一种可能的解释涉及涉及想象力的大脑区域如何协同工作。研究人员认为，对于某些人来说，协调这项活动的困难可能会在睡眠期间持续存在，而另一些人则可能会发生变化。

paras.en: Comparing brain activity in people with these different experiences could help test that idea. It could also reveal whether similar processes produce imagined sensations during waking life and dreams.
paras.zh: 比较具有不同经历的人的大脑活动可能有助于检验这个想法。它还可以揭示类似的过程是否会在清醒生活和梦中产生想象中的感觉。

paras.en: The study did not measure brain activity, so that explanation remains untested. The findings rely on participants describing their experiences and remembering their dreams. Those in the aphantasia group were also more likely to be unsure whether particular sensations occurred in their dreams. The group included some people with weak visual imagination alongside those reporting none.
paras.zh: 该研究没有测量大脑活动，因此这一解释尚未得到检验。研究结果依赖于参与者描述他们的经历并记住他们的梦想。失语症组的人也更有可能不确定他们的梦中是否出现了特定的感觉。该群体中包括一些视觉想象力较弱的人以及那些自称没有视觉想象力的人。

paras.en: Future sleep studies could bring researchers closer to the experience itself by waking participants immediately after dreams and asking what they remember.
paras.zh: 未来的睡眠研究可以通过在梦后立即唤醒参与者并询问他们记得什么来让研究人员更接近体验本身。

paras.en: Some people with aphantasia report images and sounds in dreams that they cannot call up while awake. For others, the sensations missing from waking imagination are also absent from their dreams.
paras.zh: 一些患有失语症的人报告说，他们在梦中的图像和声音在清醒时无法唤起。对于其他人来说，清醒想象中缺失的感觉在他们的梦中也不存在。

paras.en: The research has been published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: Beehives Have Built-in Immune Systems That Protect The Colony With Layers of Defense
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: The immune system of a honeybee extends well beyond the individual.
paras.zh: 蜜蜂的免疫系统远远超出了个体的范围。

paras.en: Each beehive is a marvel of insect architecture, and a new study published in ISME Communications shows just how sophisticated they are when it comes to protecting the colony from lethal outbreaks.
paras.zh: 每个蜂箱都是昆虫建筑的奇迹，《ISME Communications》发表的一项新研究表明，它们在保护蜂群免受致命疾病爆发方面是多么复杂。

paras.en: "The success of social insects relies on dense colony living, but these conditions also favor pathogen transmission," writes microbiologist Kenya Fernandes and her colleagues at the University of Sydney and the New South Wales Department of Primary Industries in Australia.
paras.zh: “社会性昆虫的成功依赖于密集的群体生活，但这些条件也有利于病原体传播，”悉尼大学和澳大利亚新南威尔士州第一产业部的微生物学家肯尼亚·费尔南德斯和她的同事写道。

paras.en: "Colonies mitigate this risk through social immunity, a coordinated system of behavioral, chemical, and immunological defenses."
paras.zh: “群体通过社会免疫（行为、化学和免疫防御的协调系统）来减轻这种风险。”

paras.en: The antimicrobial properties of honey, beeswax, and propolis (a special resin made by bees) in isolation are well-known.
paras.zh: 蜂蜜、蜂蜡和蜂胶（一种由蜜蜂制造的特殊树脂）单独的抗菌特性是众所周知的。

paras.en: But until now, we hadn't fully grasped how their spatial organization in a hive – in tandem with other immune defense strategies – adds to the colony's security against pathogens like fungi and bacteria.
paras.zh: 但直到现在，我们还没有完全掌握它们在蜂巢中的空间组织——与其他免疫防御策略相结合——如何增强蜂群抵御真菌和细菌等病原体的安全性。

paras.en: The new study found layers of immune defense are built into the colony, from the hive entrance, to the brood comb, to each bee's own guts.
paras.zh: 这项新研究发现，从蜂巢入口到蜂巢，再到每只蜜蜂自己的肠道，蜂群中都内置了多层免疫防御系统。

paras.en: "As we travel closer to the hive center, the antimicrobial defenses become more targeted, with wax comb, stored pollen and the bees' own bodies helping to filter out harmful bacteria and fungi, while encouraging helpful species," Fernandes explains.
paras.zh: “当我们靠近蜂巢中心时，抗菌防御变得更有针对性，蜡梳、储存的花粉和蜜蜂自己的身体有助于过滤掉有害细菌和真菌，同时鼓励有益的物种，”费尔南德斯解释道。

paras.en: She and her team collected samples from the hives of 24 different European honeybee (Apis mellifera) colonies based at five different apiaries in New South Wales, Australia.
paras.zh: 她和她的团队从澳大利亚新南威尔士州五个不同养蜂场的 24 个不同欧洲蜜蜂 (Apis mellifera) 群体的蜂巢中收集了样本。

paras.en: Across the hives, the scientists tested the antimicrobial and chemical contents of honey, propolis, wax, and pollen, as well as the microbiomes of the hive entrance, pollen, brood combs, and the guts of forager bees.
paras.zh: 在整个蜂巢中，科学家们测试了蜂蜜、蜂胶、蜡和花粉的抗菌和化学成分，以及蜂巢入口、花粉、蜂巢和​​采集蜜蜂肠道的微生物组。

paras.en: "Microbial communities, antimicrobial activity, and chemical composition vary predictably across hive compartments, forming a gradient from internal bee tissues to environmentally exposed hive surfaces," the team writes.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“蜂巢隔间的微生物群落、抗菌活性和化学成分可预测地变化，形成从内部蜜蜂组织到暴露于环境的蜂巢表面的梯度。”

paras.en: "These gradients are functionally coherent: compartments facing concentrated pathogen pressure, such as bee-associated tissues, exhibit more targeted activity against bacterial hive pathogens, whereas environmentally exposed materials, such as propolis, display broader, diffuse antimicrobial profiles."
paras.zh: “这些梯度在功能上是一致的：面临集中病原体压力的隔室，例如蜜蜂相关组织，对细菌蜂巢病原体表现出更有针对性的活性，而暴露在环境中的材料，例如蜂胶，则表现出更广泛、分散的抗菌特性。”

paras.en: Hives were most strongly fortified against the bacterial pathogens Paenibacillus larvae and Paenibacillus alvei, which makes sense given infection with these bacteria can completely decimate a colony.
paras.zh: 荨麻疹对细菌病原体幼虫类芽孢杆菌和蜂巢类芽孢杆菌的抵抗力最强，考虑到这些细菌的感染可以完全消灭蜂群，这是有道理的。

paras.en: The kinds of flowers available locally had a particular influence on the chemical defenses available to a colony.
paras.zh: 当地可用的花卉种类对殖民地可用的化学防御有特殊的影响。

paras.en: Defenses against fungal infections, on the other hand, were a bit less structured and weaker overall. That might be because not many fungi are actually lethal to bees: many are beneficial, and even some of the pathogenic strains are pretty tolerable.
paras.zh: 另一方面，针对真菌感染的防御系统结构较差，整体较弱。这可能是因为实际上对蜜蜂致命的真菌并不多：许多真菌都是有益的，甚至一些致病菌株也相当容易忍受。

paras.en: The bacteria associated with each layer of the colony were distinct, even though bees likely bring in microbes from flowers all the time, which suggests the hive actively filters which microbes settle where.
paras.zh: 尽管蜜蜂可能一直从花朵中带入微生物，但与蜂群每一层相关的细菌都是不同的，这表明蜂巢会主动过滤哪些微生物定居在哪里。

paras.en: Stressed colonies seemed to be a bit more disorganized in this regard.
paras.zh: 在这方面，受到压力的蜂群似乎更加混乱。

paras.en: The immune 'strength' of each colony varied depending on the location of the apiaries, hive health, and pest exposure (e.g. small hive beetles), which suggests their defense systems are quite sensitive to environmental differences.
paras.zh: 每个蜂群的免疫“强度”根据养蜂场的位置、蜂巢健康状况和害虫暴露（例如小型蜂巢甲虫）而有所不同，这表明它们的防御系统对环境差异非常敏感。

paras.en: "This shows healthy hives depend on and are influenced by healthy ecosystems," says co-author Elizabeth Frost, a bee specialist with the NSW Department of Primary Industries.
paras.zh: “这表明健康的蜂巢依赖于健康的生态系统并受其影响，”合著者、新南威尔士州第一产业部的蜜蜂专家伊丽莎白·弗罗斯特说。

paras.en: "Land clearing and intensive farming could be quietly eroding the bees' natural defenses. This builds a strong case for protecting diverse flowering habitats that support healthy hives."
paras.zh: “土地清理和集约化农业可能会悄悄侵蚀蜜蜂的自然防御。这为保护支持健康蜂巢的多样化开花栖息地提供了强有力的理由。”

paras.en: The research has been published in ISME Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 ISME Communications 上。

articles.title: Scientists shrink Archimedes’ screw to the size of a single molecule

paras.en: Scientists shrink Archimedesâ screw to the size of a single molecule
paras.zh: 科学家将阿基米德螺旋缩小到单个分子的大小

paras.en: - Scientists have built a groundbreaking molecular motor that spins in either direction using electricity, inspired by a machine invented more than 2,000 years ago. Even more remarkably, its rotation can boost electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, potentially transforming the future of molecular electronics.
paras.zh: - 受 2000 多年前发明的机器的启发，科学家们建造了一种突破性的分子马达，可以利用电力向任一方向旋转。更值得注意的是，它的旋转可以将电导率提高多达 100 倍，有可能改变分子电子学的未来。

paras.en: Scientists have developed a remarkable new molecular motor that spins when electricity passes through it. Inspired by an ancient invention, the tiny machine can even reverse its direction when the electrical voltage is switched. The achievement marks an important step toward creating working machines at the smallest possible scale.
paras.zh: 科学家们开发出了一种非凡的新型分子马达，当电流通过时它就会旋转。受到一项古老发明的启发，这个微型机器甚至可以在电压切换时反转方向。这一成就标志着朝着制造尽可能最小规模的工作机器迈出了重要一步。

paras.en: Molecular machines are widely seen as a promising next frontier in miniaturization. Nature already provides examples inside living cells, where molecular motors use energy to produce movement. Researchers have spent decades trying to recreate these remarkable biological systems artificially, and progress in this field was recognized with the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
paras.zh: 分子机器被广泛视为小型化领域有希望的下一个前沿领域。自然界已经提供了活细胞内部的例子，其中分子马达利用能量来产生运动。研究人员花了数十年的时间试图人工重建这些非凡的生物系统，该领域的进展获得了 2016 年诺贝尔化学奖的认可。

paras.en: An Ancient Invention Inspires a Molecular Motor
paras.zh: 一项古老的发明激发了分子马达

paras.en: Scientists first developed molecular motors powered directly by electricity in 2011. However, those earlier designs operated on surfaces and relied on the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope to drive their movement.
paras.zh: 科学家们于 2011 年首次开发出直接由电力驱动的分子马达。然而，那些早期的设计在表面上运行，并依赖扫描隧道显微镜的尖端来驱动它们的运动。

paras.en: The new motor takes a different approach, borrowing its basic design from the Archimedes screw, one of the oldest machines in recorded history. Traditionally used to move water uphill, this simple device relies on a rotating spiral to transport material.
paras.zh: 新电机采用了不同的方法，借鉴了阿基米德螺杆的基本设计，阿基米德螺杆是有记录的历史上最古老的机器之一。这种简单的装置传统上用于将水运上山，它依靠旋转螺旋来运输材料。

paras.en: Researchers adapted that principle to the molecular scale. Instead of moving water, their design allows electrons to travel through a spiral-shaped molecule, causing it to rotate as electrical current passes through.
paras.zh: 研究人员将该原理应用于分子尺度。他们的设计不是让水移动，而是让电子穿过螺旋形分子，使其在电流通过时旋转。

paras.en: A Tiny Molecular Screw Suspended Between Gold Tips
paras.zh: 悬挂在金尖之间的微小分子螺丝

paras.en: The motor's central component is a specially designed spiral molecule created by the research group of Prof. Michael Pittelkow at the University of Copenhagen. Measuring only a few millionths of a millimeter, the molecule can attach to gold surfaces through sulfur atoms.
paras.zh: 该电机的核心部件是由哥本哈根大学 Michael Pittelkow 教授的研究小组创建的专门设计的螺旋分子。该分子的尺寸仅为百万分之几毫米，可以通过硫原子附着在金表面。

paras.en: At the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, researchers led by Prof. Oren Tal and Dr. Anil Kumar Singh positioned individual molecules between two gold tips sharpened to atomic dimensions. By carefully changing the separation between these electrodes, the team could stretch or compress the molecular screw.
paras.zh: 在以色列魏茨曼科学研究所，奥伦·塔尔教授和阿尼尔·库马尔·辛格博士领导的研究人员将单个分子放置在两个锐化至原子尺寸的金尖之间。通过仔细改变这些电极之间的间距，研究小组可以拉伸或压缩分子螺杆。

paras.en: When the scientists applied an electrical voltage, measurements revealed that the molecule began rotating. Even more importantly, they could reverse its direction simply by changing the voltage's polarity.
paras.zh: 当科学家施加电压时，测量结果显示分子开始旋转。更重要的是，他们只需改变电压的极性就可以改变其方向。

paras.en: This represents the first demonstration of a molecular motor that is driven by electrical current, firmly connected to two metal electrodes, and capable of rotating in a controllable direction.
paras.zh: 这是分子马达的首次演示，该马达由电流驱动，牢固地连接到两个金属电极，并且能够沿可控方向旋转。

paras.en: How Electricity Makes a Single Molecule Spin
paras.zh: 电如何使单分子旋转

paras.en: The driving force comes directly from electrons traveling through the spiral molecule. As they move, they transfer angular momentum to the molecular structure, producing rotation in much the same way that moving air turns a wind turbine.
paras.zh: 驱动力直接来自穿过螺旋分子的电子。当它们移动时，它们将角动量传递给分子结构，产生旋转，就像移动的空气转动风力涡轮机一样。

paras.en: The spiral's shape determines how it responds to this flow, similar to the difference between screws with right- or left-handed threads. Once the applied voltage exceeds a certain threshold, the movement becomes continuous rotation.
paras.zh: 螺旋的形状决定了它如何响应这种流动，类似于右旋或左旋螺纹螺钉之间的差异。一旦施加的电压超过一定阈值，运动就会变成连续旋转。

paras.en: But the experiments revealed another intriguing effect. The rotating molecule conducted electricity much more efficiently than it did when stationary, raising an important question about what was happening inside the tiny machine.
paras.zh: 但实验揭示了另一个有趣的效应。旋转分子的导电效率比静止时要高得多，这引发了一个关于微型机器内部发生了什么的重要问题。

paras.en: Scientists Discover a Surprising 100-Fold Electrical Effect
paras.zh: 科学家发现令人惊讶的 100 倍电效应

paras.en: To investigate this unexpected behavior, Prof. Dr. Fabian Pauly and his PhD students Léon Martin and Yuta Ito, working at the Chair of Theoretical Physics I at the University of Augsburg, used quantum mechanical simulations on the LiCCA supercomputer.
paras.zh: 为了研究这种意想不到的行为，奥格斯堡大学理论物理一系主任 Fabian Pauly 教授及其博士生 Léon Martin 和 Yuta Ito 在 LiCCA 超级计算机上使用了量子力学模拟。

paras.en: Their calculations revealed a close relationship between the molecule's rotation and its ability to carry electrical current. Conductivity changes dramatically depending on the angle of the molecule, increasing by as much as two orders of magnitude, or 100 times, during rotation.
paras.zh: 他们的计算揭示了分子的旋转与其携带电流的能力之间的密切关系。电导率根据分子的角度发生显着变化，在旋转过程中增加多达两个数量级，即 100 倍。

paras.en: The reason turned out to be particularly surprising. Some of the molecular positions that allow electricity to pass most easily are also positions that the molecule naturally avoids when it is not moving. Rotation makes those highly conductive arrangements accessible.
paras.zh: 事实证明，原因尤其令人惊讶。一些最容易让电流通过的分子位置也是分子在不移动时自然避开的位置。旋转使这些高导电性的布置变得容易接近。

paras.en: "The surprising thing is that it is precisely the positions that the molecule avoids when at rest that conduct electricity best. It is only the rotation that makes these positions accessible," explains Léon Martin.
paras.zh: “令人惊讶的是，正是分子在静止时避开的位置导电性最好。只有旋转才能使这些位置接近，”莱昂·马丁解释道。

paras.en: The finding demonstrates that molecular motion does more than simply consume electrical energy. The movement itself can strongly influence how electricity flows through the machine.
paras.zh: 这一发现表明分子运动不仅仅是消耗电能。运动本身可以强烈影响电流通过机器的方式。

paras.en: International Collaboration Solves the Mystery
paras.zh: 国际合作解开谜团

paras.en: The researchers then worked with theoretical physicists Per Hedegård of the Niels Bohr Institute in Copenhagen and Jing-Tao Lü of Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后与哥本哈根尼尔斯玻尔研究所的理论物理学家Per Hedegård和武汉华中科技大学的Jing-Tao Lü合作。

paras.en: Using the simulation results, the scientists developed a simplified theoretical model that successfully recreated both the rotation observed in the experiments and the accompanying increase in electrical current.
paras.zh: 利用模拟结果，科学家们开发了一个简化的理论模型，成功地重现了实验中观察到的旋转以及随之而来的电流增加。

paras.en: This combination of experimental measurements and theoretical calculations was essential to understanding the mechanism. Although researchers could measure the current passing through the molecule, they needed simulations to determine what was happening at such an extraordinarily small scale.
paras.zh: 实验测量和理论计算的结合对于理解该机制至关重要。尽管研究人员可以测量通过分子的电流，但他们需要进行模拟来确定在如此小规模的情况下发生了什么。

paras.en: "In the experiment, you only see the current. Our calculations allow us to glimpse what is happening inside the nanocontact. It was only through close collaboration between experiment and theory across several countries that the mystery of the current increase could be solved," says Yuta Ito, a PhD student originally from Japan.
paras.zh: 来自日本的博士生 Yuta Ito 表示：“在实验中，你只能看到电流。我们的计算使我们能够一睹纳米接触内部发生的情况。只有通过多个国家的实验和理论之间的密切合作，才能解开电流增加的谜团。”

paras.en: A New Frontier for Molecular Electronics
paras.zh: 分子电子学的新领域

paras.en: The achievement could eventually contribute to the development of molecular electronic components and technologies involving spintronics, which uses properties of electrons beyond their electrical charge. It may also offer possibilities for microfluidic systems, which manipulate extremely small quantities of fluids.
paras.zh: 这一成就最终可能有助于分子电子元件和涉及自旋电子学技术的发展，自旋电子学利用电子超越其电荷的特性。它还可能为微流体系统提供可能性，微流体系统可以操纵极少量的流体。

paras.en: Beyond these potential applications, the motor provides scientists with a new way to investigate physical processes at the atomic scale. Its ability to convert electricity into controlled rotation, while allowing that rotation to influence electrical current, introduces a new principle for designing extraordinarily small machines.
paras.zh: 除了这些潜在的应用之外，该电机还为科学家提供了一种在原子尺度上研究物理过程的新方法。它能够将电力转换为受控旋转，同时允许旋转影响电流，为设计超小型机器引入了新原理。

paras.en: "We have shown that an electric current can be used to generate a directed rotation and that this rotation, in turn, controls the current. This is a new operating principle for machines at the very limits of miniaturization," explains Pauly.
paras.zh: “我们已经证明，电流可以用来产生定向旋转，而这种旋转反过来又控制电流。对于处于小型化极限的机器来说，这是一种新的操作原理，”保利解释道。

paras.en: The work at the University of Augsburg received funding from the German Research Foundation (DFG) through Collaborative Research Center (SFB) 1585 (project number 492723217). The computational research was conducted using the University of Augsburg's LiCCA supercomputer (DFG project number 499211671).
paras.zh: 奥格斯堡大学的这项工作通过合作研究中心 (SFB) 1585（项目号 492723217）获得了德国研究基金会 (DFG) 的资助。计算研究是使用奥格斯堡大学的 LiCCA 超级计算机（DFG 项目号 499211671）进行的。

paras.en: Additional support for the collaborating institutions came from the European Research Council (ERC, Horizon 2020, Grant 864008), the Israel Science Foundation (2129/23), the Minerva Foundation, the Villum Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), the National Key Research and Development Program of China, and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
paras.zh: 对合作机构的额外支持来自欧洲研究理事会（ERC，Horizo​​n 2020，Grant 864008）、以色列科学基金会（2129/23）、密涅瓦基金会、Villum基金会、诺和诺德基金会、丹麦独立研究基金（DFF）、中国国家重点研发计划和中国国家自然科学基金委员会。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Augsburg. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由奥格斯堡大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。
